Knowledge-base integrity audit and repair: OWL consistency does not guarantee that the rule cards are free of domain errors, so an automated audit (eval/audit.py) checks for: (a) contradictory rules equal to a positive rule of the same genus; (b) mandatory rules conflicting with another mandatory or diagnostic rule on the same character; (c) negated rule texts with positive mappings (polarity screen); (d) character–state pairs counted more than once within a genus, directly or through implication (by two diagnostic or supporting rules, or by a mandatory and a diagnostic rule); (e) unmapped mandatory rules; (f) genera without a scoring diagnostic rule; (g) tree answers outside the controlled vocabulary; (h) characters queried again along one path; and (i) genera not assigned to exactly one module. Two logged scripts that operate only on rule texts and trees, never on evaluation outcomes, repaired the findings (eval/apply_audit_fixes.py, 67 mapping edits; eval/bind_tree_vocabulary.py, 7 answer bindings): each rule is re-mapped to the state its text states or, where the vocabulary cannot express a qualifier (e.g., “low trochospiral” or “Lacazina-type pillar pattern absent”), returned to a non-scoring hint instead of a misleading proxy; five off-vocabulary tree answers were bound to controlled states (e.g., “flattened/sigmoid serial organization” to the state used for the same concept in the rule card of Rzehakina), and two complement answers became routing answers resolved by the next character-bound question. Across the nine categories, the audit counts changed from 17, 10, 4, 25, 27, 18, 7, 11, and 0 to 0, 0, 3, 0, 28, 2, 0, 11, and 0. The three remaining polarity flags are not inverted mappings on inspection; the mandatory rule of Pseudolacazina that states alternatives on two characters (M4, “partitions and/or pillars”) is now evaluated disjunctively (Section VI-A); and (f) first rose from 18 to 28 when diagnostic mappings that only repeated a mandatory pair or misrepresented the text were removed. Three of the 18 genera originally lacking a scoring diagnostic rule received a literal mapping (Hauerina; Orbitoclypeus and Nemkovella, via the embryonic-apparatus state of the corresponding tree answer). A second logged pass ([TBD: script]) then mapped the diagnostic statements of all but two of the remaining genera literally to the anatomical structure and state that their text names in the existing vocabulary; statements that remained ambiguous were kept as hints rather than made scoring to clear the audit, so that two genera ([TBD: names]) still lack a scoring diagnostic rule. The repaired master files, every edit with its textual basis, and the item-by-item audit listings before and after repair are given in Supplementary Material S9.

For each of the 104 root-to-leaf paths, every character-bound answer sets its character to the answered state or to the state of its explicit binding (with any implied states), CHR_01 is set to the module, and every other character is NOT_OBSERVABLE; where a character is queried twice along a path (audit item (h)), [TBD: rule of the repaired release for combining the two answers; previously the later answer overwrote the earlier one]; Algorithm 1 then scores this set, recording the rank of the leaf genus (ties sharing the rank), its exclusion, and the confidence state. As the 22 composite questions contribute no observation, the test is conservative: it measures how much discriminating information of each path the rule cards express. A leaf excluded by its own path indicates a tree–rule contradiction; CONFIRMED_GENUS for another genus indicates overconfidence. Table XII gives the results after the repair of Section IV-B.

The repair mainly removed overconfidence (Table XII): CONFIRMED_GENUS outputs fell from 48 to 27 while the share identifying the leaf genus rose from 29% to 70%, and no path excludes its own leaf genus any longer (17 before repair); unique first ranks changed from 24 to [TBD] and tied ones from 10 to [TBD], because genera previously separated only by diagnostic proxies now share their mandatory evidence and are reported as CANDIDATE_GENUS sets. In an intermediate state of the repair, 16 of 19 excluded leaves were porcelaneous, and 11 of these traced to one node: the lacazinid and complex milioline branch is reached through the answer “simple chambers” (CHR_10 = SIMPLE) at question PORC_Q2, whereas the rule cards of Lacazina, Lacazinella, Pseudolacazina, Periloculina, and Idalina require internal subdivision or contradict simple chambers. Part of these contradictions arose because a character queried twice along a path with different meanings (audit item (h)) had its first answer overwritten by the second; [TBD: how the repaired release resolves the PORC_Q2 conflict and the repeated queries]. The eight CONFIRMED_GENUS outputs that name a genus other than the leaf are listed per path in Supplementary Material S9 and form the work list of the next release.

Implementation checks: All ten competency queries matched the independently derived answers (Section IV-B), and the [TBD] API tests, including the reproduction of Tables XI and XII, and seven regression tests of the evaluation scripts (RBO properties, tie credit, frozen-input checksums, audit targets, pairing of the simulation, threshold invariance of the rankings, and equivalence of the offline and application scorers) pass on the repaired release, establishing the internal consistency of the implementation.

The rankings were stable (Table XV): no weight variant reduced the path RBO below 0.93 or changed Acc@1 by more than 2.4 points. The reversed hierarchy (S2) changed the top-1 genus most often and raised Acc@3 at the expense of Acc@1, whereas S1 and S2 issued far fewer CONFIRMED_GENUS outputs with a higher share of correct ones, i.e., a more conservative but less informative engine. The thresholds do not alter scores and leave every ranking unchanged (RBO = 1 for all 27 settings); they act only on the confidence states: τNM had no effect because no path reached NO_MATCH_WITHIN_CORE_TAXA, δ = 2 and δ = 3 reduced the CONFIRMED_GENUS outputs from 27 to [TBD] and [TBD], and τobs = 3 reduced the coverage from 85.6% to 75.0% and Acc@1 to 21.3%. On the drafted sheets, Acc@1 stayed between 3.2% and 3.6% under every setting. No setting dominated the default, which was therefore retained; selecting weights on these development data would overfit them.

context: Results: For the five remaining profiles, A0 ranked the described genus first in none and reached a tie-aware top-3 agreement (6) of 50% [TBD: B1, coverage, and reference exclusions]. Five descriptions that also guided the design of the character vocabulary are neither independent nor numerous enough to estimate accuracy, but they show that the agreement on rule-consistent inputs (Sections VIII-B to VIII-E) does not yet carry over to published descriptions, so accuracy on independent material remains open. The ontology file, character definitions, decision trees, rule cards, evaluation scripts, and application code are available at https://github.com/datkanber/foraminifera-fossil under the MIT License (code) and CC BY 4.0 (ontology and data). The results were computed on the repaired release in Supplementary Material S9, which supersedes commit 1e12fb5fc2c32e5d042f4f322c823c50dcda59b6 and records SHA-256 checksums of all master files, scripts, and outputs; npm test in the api directory runs the [TBD] unit and regression tests (including the reproduction of Tables XI and XII), and the scripts listed in S9 reproduce the offline evaluation without calling an external model. No project DOI is given because the v1.0 release and its Zenodo archive are not yet published. The ontology uses the persistent IRI https://w3id.org/foram-ontology (version IRI https://w3id.org/foram-ontology/1.0), in line with the FAIR principles [64]. The running system is available at https://geoknow.asrlab.cloud/. WoRMS records are subject to the terms of that service [39]. Supplementary Materials S1–S8 contain the knowledge-base inventory, WoRMS lookup, and pre-repair audit (S1); competency-query executions (S2); the OWL file and JSON trees (S3); the VLM prompt, controller, scoring snapshot, and frozen configuration (S4); panel sources, crop coordinates, checksums, and licenses (S5); pre-repair internal paths and ablations (S6); panel-level VLM responses and metrics (S7); and stratified results (S8). S9 holds the repaired master files, audit and repair logs, and all present results; S10 holds the protocol of the blinded expert review of LLM-drafted observations and of the planned confirmatory study, moved there from the main text, together with its shareable records (drafting prompt and configuration, per-case state counts of the pilot drafts, archived A0 and B1 code with checksums, and test logs) but no observations, reference labels, or participant data; the pilot images and raw drafts are withheld until the pilot review is locked. The panels are crops of CC BY 4.0 publications [2], [58], [59], redistributed with attribution and a statement of modification; the author portrait is not covered by this license.
